reps.resume: The lifter performs a single conventional deadlift with a rounded upper and lower back, maintaining a smooth bar path and a solid lockout.

observations.hip_height: At setup between 3.90s and 4.30s, the hips are positioned vertically below the shoulders and above the knees, forming a clear angle at both joints. The camera angle is from a three-quarter side view, which allows a clear view of these relative heights.
observations.shoulders_over_bar: At 3.90s to 4.30s, the shoulder joints are positioned directly above the vertical line of the barbell, with the arms hanging vertically down to the bar.
observations.bar_over_midfoot: At setup between 3.90s and 4.30s, the barbell is positioned directly against the shins, with no visible gap between the bar and the lower leg.
observations.lumbar_at_setup: In the close-up frames at 3.90s, 4.10s, and 4.30s, the lower back shows a convex curvature, bending away from the front of the body.
observations.thoracic_at_setup: At 3.90s to 4.30s, the upper back exhibits a rounded, convex shape, with the shoulders positioned forward.
observations.arms_long: From 3.90s to 5.10s, the arms remain fully extended in a straight line from the shoulders to the hands, with no bending at the elbows.
observations.slack_pull: Between 4.30s and 4.50s, the lifter applies upward force gradually, tensioning the body and the barbell before the plates leave the floor.
observations.brace: At 3.90s to 4.30s, the abdominal wall is seen expanding outward against the lifting belt, maintaining this expansion as the lift begins.
observations.hip_vs_shoulder_rise: From 4.30s to 4.70s, the hips and shoulders move upward at the same rate, maintaining a constant torso angle relative to the floor.
observations.jerky_start: At 4.30s to 4.50s, the barbell lifts off the floor in a smooth, continuous motion without any sudden jerks or rapid shifts in position.
observations.bar_left_floor: At 4.50s, the barbell is clearly elevated above the platform, indicating it has left the floor.
observations.past_the_knees: Between 4.70s and 4.90s, the barbell travels vertically past the knees in a straight line without any forward deviation or contact with the kneecaps.
observations.bar_leg_contact: From 4.50s to 5.10s, the barbell remains in continuous contact with the shins and thighs as it rises.
observations.lumbar_under_load: In the close-up frames from 4.30s to 4.90s, the convex curvature of the lower back remains constant, showing no change in shape under the load.
observations.thoracic_under_load: From 4.30s to 4.90s, the rounded shape of the upper back remains stable and unchanged throughout the pull.
observations.knee_valgus: The three-quarter side camera angle makes it difficult to clearly observe any inward or outward lateral movement of both knees.
observations.hitch: From 4.50s to 5.10s, the barbell rises in a single, continuous upward motion without stalling or resting on the thighs.
observations.asymmetry: The side-angle view prevents a direct comparison of the left and right sides of the body to assess lateral symmetry.
observations.lean_back: At 5.10s and 5.50s, the lifter stands with the hips fully extended and the torso in a vertical position, without leaning backward.
observations.shrug: At 5.10s and 5.50s, the shoulders remain in a depressed position, with no upward movement toward the ears.
observations.lockout_completion: At 5.10s and 5.50s, the knees and hips are fully extended, and the lifter is standing completely upright.
observations.descent_control: The provided frames jump from 5.50s to 8.40s, omitting the descent phase of the lift.
observations.rep_transition: Only a single repetition is shown in the sequence, with no subsequent repetitions initiated.
